Comment on five (5) of the items (a)–(j): (a) “The angel of the Lord appeared to the woman and said, ‘You shall conceive and bear a son’.” (Judges 13:3). (4 marks) (b) “Now appoint for us a king to govern us like all the nations.” (1 Samuel 8:5). (4 marks) (c) “Then Nathan said to David, ‘You are the man!’.” (2 Samuel 12:7). (4 marks) (d) “Then Elijah said, ‘How long will you go limping between two different opinions?’.” (1 Kings 18:21). (4 marks) (e) “Because Manasseh king of Judah has committed these abominations… I am bringing such evil upon Jerusalem.” (2 Kings 21:11-12). (4 marks) (f) “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory.” (Isaiah 6:3). (4 marks) (g) “The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately corrupt.” (Jeremiah 17:9). (4 marks) (h) “Son of man, can these bones live?” (Ezekiel 37:3). (4 marks) (i) “For they sow the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind.” (Hosea 8:7). (4 marks) (j) “Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit, says the Lord of hosts.” (Zechariah 4:6). (4 marks)
Describe the military leadership of Deborah and explain her importance in Israel’s history. (20 marks)
Analyze the achievements and weaknesses of King David’s reign. (20 marks)
Examine the reasons for the fall of the Northern Kingdom of Israel in 722 B.C. (20 marks)
Explain Isaiah’s teaching on the Messianic hope with reference to Isaiah chapters 7–11. (20 marks)
Discuss Hosea’s marriage to Gomer as a symbol of God’s relationship with Israel. (20 marks)
